status: Investigation complete; functional soak passed; memory plateau not established.
conclusions: No accumulation of native bridges or view hosts was observed in four heap snapshots; native allocated malloc memory remained approximately 46-48 MiB.
The separate five-minute workload returned to approximately startup managed-heap size after explicit collection, supporting delayed collection as a contributor to observed memory growth.
The unforced fifteen-minute run did not reach a memory plateau. This experiment does not prove the absence of a leak or establish indefinite memory stability.

unresolved.finding: macOS leaks reported small unattributed malloc blocks; no allocation stack logging was enabled.
unresolved.attribution: Unknown; not established as NativeChannels allocations.

unresolved: Android, iOS and Windows long-running memory behavior were not measured in this investigation.
limitations: One Mac Catalyst ARM64 development run using local mobile packages.
External heap inspections briefly pause/fault process memory; capture times are recorded separately.
No forced garbage collection; process footprint is not isolated NativeChannels heap usage.
leaks output includes unattributed small malloc blocks; no allocation stacks were collected.
These observations do not establish absence of leaks on all platforms.
Forced collection was diagnostic only, after a separate shorter workload; it is not a production workaround or evidence that the entire fifteen-minute footprint is reclaimable.
